blindSummary:
This country is among the most severe environments for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct is criminalised nationally under a 2014 prohibition law (14 years, applies to all including tourists), and 12 states that operate parallel religious-law penal codes prescribe the death penalty for male same-sex conduct. An openly transgender short-video creator known by a neighbourhood nickname was found beaten and dead on a highway in the capital; police misgendered her in death and, six months later, no one has been arrested. Police have beaten LGBTQ+ people for "looking gay" — the 2014 law has been described as a "weaponised" law — and dating-app lure gangs use geolocation apps to draw victims into assault and robbery. A foreign government's travel advisory warns LGBT+ travellers to this country of arrest, violence, and death-penalty risks.

A proposed cross-dressing ban (not yet passed) would criminalise gender expression in public. Trans identity is NOT explicitly criminalised nationally (the 2014 law targets same-sex conduct), and the violence concentrates against local communities rather than tourists. But the religious-law death penalty, the trans-specific killing with impunity, the police brutality, and the foreign advisory make the practical risk extreme.
blindOutOfScope: Insurgency-related terrorism in parts of the country, kidnapping, and violent crime affect all travellers in many regions; only trans-specific risk is assessed here.
blindTangential: The 2014 prohibition law (14 years, applies to tourists) and the death penalty under religious-law penal codes in 12 states are direct risks for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active; dating-app lure gangs are a direct app-user risk.
blindSourceSummaries: Foreign public broadcaster (Aug 2024): a transgender short-video creator from this country found dead - her beaten body was found along a capital highway hours after posting about going to see her boyfriend; she had previously expressed fears for her life. Police described her as 'a man fully dressed in female clothing'; same-sex relationships are criminalised here and perceived-gay video creators face homophobic abuse online.

Independent news site (Feb 2025): reporting on what it is like to be queer in this country, centred on the creator's killing; six months later no suspects charged; the 2014 same-sex-marriage prohibition act reinforced colonial-era criminalisation; transphobia and homophobia are common with no legal protections.

National news outlet (Aug 2026): a foreign government's latest travel advice for this country warns LGBT+ travellers of arrest, violence, attacks, blackmail and intimidation - same-sex activity illegal with up to 14 years' imprisonment; some states operate under religious penal codes which can prescribe the death penalty; the 2014 act provides lengthy sentences extending to those who arrange, conduct or attend events perceived as same-sex weddings.

Foreign daily (March 2025): LGBTQ+ people from this country recount police abuses under the 'weaponised' law - a 24-year-old man was stopped, beaten and forced to pay a bribe for 'looking gay'; the law creates a climate of hostility making LGBTQ+ people vulnerable to violations by police and the public.

Independent newsroom (Aug 2024): 10 years of this country's anti-LGBTQ law - the 2014 act has fuelled violence, extortion and discrimination far beyond its scope, presenting LGBTQI persons as criminals; criminalisation blocks access to redress and justice; job prospects harmed; attacks increased since the law passed.

Independent newsroom (April 2024): LGBTQ+ people in this country battle dating-app traps - violent entrapment via geolocation apps; victims are beaten, filmed, and blackmailed with threats to out them to family; community members fight back with exposure forums and sting operations.

A foreign home ministry's official country-of-origin information and assessment (June 2025, updated April 2026) for asylum claims, covering sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics in this country.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying wire-service report (Sept 2022) covers trans people in this country fearing proposals to criminalise cross-dressing.

International human-rights organisation report (Oct 2016) on the impact of the 2014 same-sex-marriage prohibition act - its scope is far wider than marriage: it bans cohabitation, 'public show of same sex amorous relationship', and gay organisations (10-14 years); police torture and arbitrary arrests; vigilante groups added homosexuality to their 'terms of reference'.
